transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. Um, it's really nice to meet you. I hope it's okay that I'm here. I... well, I guess I came in because I've been having a little bit of trouble lately. It's probably nothing, really, but... I've been hearing things. Like, voices. They sound just as clear as if somebody were standing right there in my little studio apartment with me. They call my name, and... they tell me my work is being judged. Even when the house is completely quiet and I know nobody is there. I know it sounds silly, and I'm really trying to ignore it, but it's been a little hard. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, recently?

Oh, no, not really. I mean, I have my moments where I might feel a little tired after a long shift at work—being on your feet all day can do that, you know? But I wouldn't say I've been feeling down or depressed like that. I try to stay positive and keep a smile on my face for the people I help. I hope that's the right answer... I just haven't really noticed feeling sad like that. Is it okay if I haven't been feeling depressed?
Have you had any head injury, seizure, or other medical illness around the time these voices started?

Oh, no. No head injuries or anything like that. I've always been pretty careful, and... well, I haven't been sick with anything else, either. I mean, maybe just a little cold here and there, but nothing serious. No seizures or anything scary like that. I'm pretty healthy, all things considered. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that I haven't had any other medical problems?
About how long have you been hearing these voices?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while. I kept hoping it would just sort of fade away on its own, you know? But... it's been about nine months now. Nine months of hearing them, and having this... this awful feeling that my work is being watched and judged. I really tried not to make a fuss about it for a long time, because I didn't want anyone to think I wasn't doing a good job with my clients. I hope it's okay that I waited this long to say something... I probably should have come in sooner, shouldn't I?
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other recreational drugs around the time the voices started?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I... I don't really drink, and I would never touch any kind of drugs or anything like that. I take my job taking care of my clients very seriously, so I always make sure I have a completely clear head. I would never do anything to jeopardize them or my work. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to assure you that I'm very responsible when it comes to that sort of stuff. Did I answer that okay? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you had any fixed beliefs that other people think are false or strange, like being watched, followed, controlled, or specially targeted?

Well... um... I know it probably sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud. I really don't want you to think badly of me, but... yes. I did kind of get it in my head that... well, that the other home-care agency, and even some people from the library, were watching me. 

They were watching my paintings, and my client papers, trying to steal a chance that was meant for me. People kept telling me it made absolutely no sense, and I tried so hard to listen to them and not make a fuss about it... but I just still knew they were doing it. It felt so real to me. 

I hope you don't think I'm too strange for thinking those things? I just want to be completely honest with you so I can be a good patient. Did I explain that alright?
Have you ever had a period of at least one week where you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, or were much more active than usual?

Well, um... I guess there have been times, yes. I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad person, but... sometimes I get this feeling that's just so bright and... and big, you know? Like I'm chosen for something special, and all my plans are just too grand for a place like Greenville to even hold them. I get so much done, and I barely even need to sleep. 

But then... oh, I hate to admit this, it's so embarrassing... sometimes it flips, and I get so irritable. I'll snap really hard at someone over the tiniest little thing. Like if one of my clients just asks me to repeat myself, I'll get so short with them. I always feel terrible about it afterward, because I really do love my clients and I want to be good to them. 

I try so hard to keep it all under control, I really do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too awful... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Have you ever had a full episode of depression or mania that lasted for a substantial part of the same time you were hearing voices or having these beliefs?

Well... um... yes, I think so. I really hope this doesn't make me sound completely out of my mind, but... yes, they did happen at the same time. 

When I was having that... that really bright time, you know, when I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night and I was so focused on pushing my big plans for my art and my care work... that was also when I was hearing the voices in my studio. And it was right then that I felt so absolutely sure that those people were watching my work and trying to take my chances away. 

It was all happening right at the same time. I tried to just focus on my grand plans and ignore the rest of it, I really did. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you all this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture so you can help me... am I doing okay?
